newsitem.title: UK: Britain carried out germ tests in London - paper.
newsitem.headline: Britain carried out germ tests in London - paper.

text.p: British Defence Ministry scientists carried out secret germ warfare tests in central London and southern England between 1963 and 1977, a Sunday newspaper reported.
The Sunday Telegraph said "simulants" of biological warfare agents were exposed in public places in London such as Waterloo Bridge and the Thames embankment and along the south coast.
Simulants are organisms designed to mimic the behaviour of virulent biological warfare germs without having the same harmful effects.

The newspaper said official documents showed the tests were carried out in strict secrecy, with one senior government official warning that "knowledge of them by unauthorised persons could be politically embarrassing."

It said Defence Secretary Michael Portillo disclosed details of the tests in a letter to a member of parliament for the main opposition Labour Party in which he said the simulants used were "judged to present no risk to public health."

But it also quoted leading microbiologists as saying that some of the simulants could cause pneumonia, septicaemia or opthalmitis in vulnerable individuals such as young children, old people or those already ill.
Portillo said the tests were carried out to "determine the effect of environmental conditions on the viability of organisms."
The Defence Ministry confirmed the contents of Portillo's letter but said it would not comment further for the time being.
